subject: Pilot runway & evaluation roadmap — alignment and next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@aria.ai>, Aria Solutions POC <poc@aria.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway & evaluation roadmap — alignment and next steps

Hi Aisha / Aria team —

Thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier. Quick written recap so we all have the same frame going into a pilot: appreciate you walking us through the current workflows — below are the pain points, the goals you stated, and a proposed minimal pilot runway for validation. Please flag anything we missed.

Pain points (what you said)
- High latency on customer-facing summarization (avg 2.8s/token) causing UX drop-offs
- Cost unpredictability at peak traffic; engineering has limited observability into per-route token spend
- Model hallucinations on rare legal/contract queries leading to manual review overhead

Stated goals for the pilot
- Reduce median response latency by ~30% for the primary summarization route
- Demonstrate predictable unit cost below your target of $0.0025/token at 90th percentile
- Reduce manual review rate for legal queries by 60% (improve precision on ground-truth prompts)

Proposed pilot scope (45-day runway — quick validation phase)
- Duration: 45 days (30-day active eval + 15-day buffer for edge cases)
- Workloads: two routes — summarization (prod subset) and legal-query assistant (internal dataset)
- Metrics: median latency, p95 latency, cost-per-token (observed), hallucination rate on curated eval set
- Prompt/eval plan: we’ll deliver an initial prompt_seed_set.csv (attached) and a short eval harness for your legal prompts

Owners & roles
- Aria: Aisha Kumar (product lead) — data access and final success signoff
- Redwood: Ben Carter (Sales) — commercial owner; Karthik Iyer (Solutions Eng) — technical lead; Sofia Ivanova (SE) — pilot orchestration and evals

Access & immediate asks (to unblock week 1)
1) Provide an S3 read role for the prod-sample bucket (minimal subset) — scoped credentials or temp access ok
2) Share the security questionnaire doc or point us to the SOC2 evidence folder if available
3) Confirm a technical kickoff slot next week (we suggested Tue/Thu mornings PT)

Attachments included: pilot_scope_v1.pdf (scope + milestone calendar), prompt_seed_set.csv (seed prompts/eval set), redwood-onboarding-playbook.odt (ops checklist).

Next step: if this aligns, we’ll lock the kickoff date and Ben will issue a short commercial confirmation (trial terms + success credits). Karthik and I will draft the initial eval slate and smoke-tests once we have S3 access.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@aria.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot runway & evaluation roadmap — alignment and next steps

Thanks Sofia — this is very helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data: we can provide a scoped S3 role for a sanitized sample of the prod logs by Friday EOD. We will need a short data handling agreement (one pager) before cross-account access.
2) Security: we do have a SOC2 folder (internal Docs) but compliance needs a point-by-point response to our vendor questionnaire — can your security team fill the attached questionnaire?
3) Success metric nuance: for the legal assistant, we measure "manual escalate" (binary) rather than hallucination rate; we'd like to run both but signoff will be on manual escalate reduction.

We can do a technical kickoff on Tue, Nov 10 at 10:00 PT — works for our engineers and product lead.

Also please confirm whether Redwood can route fallback traffic to a smaller model during the pilot if we hit capacity spikes (cost/latency protection). That’ll be important for our platform team.

Aisha Kumar
Head of Product, Aria Solutions
aisha.kumar@aria.ai | (212) 555-8842
